record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Identify the correct or 'natural' form of a Lieb-Thirring inequality for complex-valued potentials, since currently available sum-of-eigenvalues bounds do not yet determine the right general statement.

evidence.quote: Despite these works, the natural form of the Lieb–Thirring inequality in the complex case seems to be unclear; see [20] for a counterexample in d = 1 to one possible form.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and consider the Schrödinger operator $H_V = -\Delta + V$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, where the potential $V:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{C}$ is complex-valued and decays at infinity (e.g., $V\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for suitable $p$). Let $\{\lambda_j(V)\}_j$ denote the discrete (in general complex) eigenvalues of $H_V$, repeated according to algebraic multiplicity.

In the self-adjoint case ($V$ real-valued), the classical Lieb–Thirring inequality asserts that for $\gamma\ge 1/2$ if $d=1$, $\gamma>0$ if $d=2$, and $\gamma\ge 0$ if $d\ge 3$, there exists a constant $L_{\gamma,d}$ such that
$$\sum_j |\lambda_j(V)|^\gamma \;\le\; L_{\gamma,d}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V_-(x)^{\gamma+d/2}\,dx,$$
where $V_-=\max(-V,0)$.

Problem. Determine the correct "natural" extension of the Lieb–Thirring inequality to complex-valued potentials: namely, find a bound of the form
$$\sum_j F\bigl(\lambda_j(V)\bigr) \;\le\; C_{\gamma,d}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |V(x)|^{\gamma+d/2}\,dx$$
(or another comparable functional of the eigenvalues) which holds for all complex $V$ in the appropriate $L^p$ class, and which reduces to the classical inequality when $V$ is real and non-positive. In particular, identify the correct weight function $F$ on $\mathbb{C}$ (depending on $\gamma$ and $d$) and the admissible range of exponents $\gamma$ for which such an inequality holds with a finite constant.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2021–2025) have ruled out some natural candidate forms via counter-examples (e.g., the Demuth–Hansmann–Katriel conjecture was disproved in dimension 1 and the disproof extended to higher dimensions), and optimal Lieb–Thirring–type inequalities for Schrödinger and Jacobi operators with complex potentials have been established with weighted eigenvalue sums. Nevertheless, identification of the single "correct" natural form in full generality remains an active and only partially settled question.

status_evidence.title: On Lieb-Thirring inequalities for multidimensional Schrödinger operators with complex potentials
status_evidence.snippet: An open problem by Demuth, Hansmann, and Katriel has been solved by a counter-example; the 1D counter-example was generalized to higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: A natural candidate form of the complex Lieb–Thirring inequality has been disproved in all dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Lieb–Thirring type inequalities for Schrödinger and Jacobi operators with complex potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Eigenvalue power sums are bounded by the L^p norm of the potential, with each term weighted by a function in contrast to the self-adjoint case.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal weighted Lieb–Thirring inequalities for complex potentials have been recently obtained.

status_evidence.title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: Recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: The natural form of the Lieb–Thirring inequality in the complex case seems to be unclear.
status_evidence.claim: The correct general form for complex potentials remains unsettled.
